A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APPLE research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V3 reports original evaluations of APPLE and baselines on five benchmarks, with learning curves, prediction metrics, and supplementary PPO/HAM experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds CIFAR-10 results, component ablations, sparse-supervision experiments, and a downstream control experiment.

M1.justification: The main APPLE architecture, SAC/CrossQ adaptations, and joint optimization procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds a specific adaptation for missing labels: storing an availability flag and masking the prediction loss, tested using only terminal supervision.

E1.justification: V4 retains the five original benchmarks and adds active classification of natural CIFAR-10 images using local glimpses (Appendices B.5 and C.6). CircleSquareHideAndSeek additionally introduces a downstream control objective requiring class-dependent approach or avoidance, extending coverage beyond property prediction alone.

E2.justification: V4 adds comparisons against APPLE-GRID, APPLE-SAC-PURE-RL, and APPLE-CrossQ-PURE-RL on CircleSquare, plus APPLE-CrossQ-NO-PRED on HideAndSeek (Figures 16–19). These introduce fixed-search and prediction-supervision controls beyond the retained HAM, random-policy, and PPO comparisons.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 1M-step component comparisons, terminal-only prediction supervision, cumulative base-return evaluation for HideAndSeek, and CIFAR-10 test-split evaluation through 2.5M steps. The original benchmark protocols are largely retained; changed curves do not establish reruns. Figure 18 leaves the sparse experiment's duration ambiguous: its caption states 1M steps, while its axis ends at 0.25M.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds direct plotted evidence about transformer versus LSTM backbones, supervised prediction versus pure RL, and learned versus grid-search exploration. It also tests terminal-only supervision and the usefulness of prediction supervision for downstream control. The earlier long-run PPO/HAM analyses are retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds and one-standard-deviation bands for the main comparisons; v4 uses the same practice for CIFAR-10. No increased replication or new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure is documented. Changes to plotted means and uncertainty bands concern results.

E6.justification: V4 adds CIFAR-10 final accuracies of 76%, 73%, and 67% for APPLE-SAC, APPLE-CrossQ, and APPLE-RND, respectively, plus the new ablation and task-variant results. Some retained curves also change: notably, HAM rises substantially above chance in v3 Figure 9 but remains near chance in v4 Figure 14 under the same stated setting. Main-text numerical summaries remain unchanged, and the reason for these curve revisions is unspecified.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the prediction factor from pi(o|h) to pi(y|o) and adds transition and target-conditional factors to the trajectory distribution. The main objective, gradient decomposition, and appendix derivation are retained. Appendices C.3–C.4 introduce a masked-loss definition and downstream reward; the latter's distance signs conflict with the stated approach/avoid objective.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows effectiveness 'regardless of the task' to effectiveness on several tasks as a step toward generality, and explicitly foregrounds the unified formulation as a contribution. It also qualifies the primary scope as perception itself. The central claim of jointly learning perception and exploration across classification and regression remains.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands interpretation through explanations of the component ablations, qualified conclusions about sparse supervision and downstream control, and discussion of tactile sim-to-real obstacles. Section 5 adds interpretations of less recognizable digit-exploration behavior, while Appendix H distinguishes within-episode information gathering from curiosity-driven policy training. The existing sample-efficiency and single-sensor limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 promises a future code release upon acceptance; v4 instead directs readers to source-code access through the project page. V4 also documents CIFAR-10 observation/action processing and sparse-label bookkeeping. Table 1, hardware specifications, replay-buffer details, and training-time disclosures are substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens coverage of imitation learning, visual active perception, scene understanding, and haptic curiosity. New positioning relates APPLE to internally rewarded RL, while Appendix H contrasts it with RND and ICM. The conclusion also introduces relevant sim-to-real literature; these are substantive additions beyond publication-metadata updates to existing citations.

P1.justification: V4 tightens the introduction, rewrites portions of related work, reorganizes contribution bullets, and adds acknowledgments. Supplementary experiments previously embedded in environment details are grouped into a dedicated Further Experiments appendix. The main section sequence and much of the methods/results prose remain intact; much of the expansion consists of new scientific content.

P2.justification: V4 adds a CIFAR-10 illustration and substantial new graphical evidence for component ablations, sparse supervision, downstream control, and CIFAR-10 performance (Figures 13, 15–19, and 21). Existing plots are resized and repositioned, including the old PPO and MHSB figures becoming Figures 14 and 20. Table 1 retains its structure.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses an important evidential gap by directly testing supervised prediction and learned exploration against pure-RL and grid-search controls, while CIFAR-10 extends support to natural images. These additions strengthen the central methodological case, and expanded research positioning clarifies the contribution. Unexplained revisions to retained curves and the HideAndSeek reward/prose contradiction limit confidence in specific results, but do not outweigh the substantial gain in component validation and coverage.
